title: Comparing the Lee-Yang gap with the mass gap in the sub-critical planar Ising model
authors: Noam Borgnia, Jui-Hui Chung, Jacob Shapiro
abstract: We prove that the subcritical mass gap is comparable to the Lee-Yang gap over free-boundary square boxes raised to the power $8/15$. Random-current moment bounds, a correlation inequality and a finite block expansion give the upper bound. The lower bound follows from the Lee-Yang product, the susceptibility and the critical magnetization. We also obtain uniform factorial bounds on the field derivatives of the pressure.
summary: This theoretical paper rigorously compares the subcritical mass gap and the Lee-Yang gap for the planar Ising model. Using sophisticated tools like random-current moment bounds and correlation inequalities, the authors establish a precise power-law relationship between these two fundamental spectral quantities near the critical point. This work represents a significant mathematical advance in the understanding of phase transitions in lattice models.
main_problem: The paper aims to rigorously compare the subcritical mass gap ($m_ eta$) with the Lee-Yang gap ($L_ eta$) in the planar Ising model.
main_result: The authors prove that the mass gap and Lee-Yang gap are comparable near criticality, specifically showing $c L^{8/15}/ eta \le m_ eta \le C L^{8/15}/ eta$ for the subcritical regime.
method: The proof combines advanced techniques including random-current moment bounds, correlation inequalities, finite block expansions, and analysis of the Lee-Yang product zeros.
model_or_system: The system is the planar, $\mathbb{Z}_2$ Ising model, studied in the sub-critical regime ($0 <  eta <  eta_c$). The analysis extends to the Random Field Ising Model (RFIM) in some parts.
key_observables: Mass gap ($m_ eta$), Lee-Yang gap ($L_ eta$), infinite-volume susceptibility ($\chi_ eta$), and the partition function $Z_{ eta,\Lambda}(h)$.
important_parameters: The critical inverse temperature $ eta_c$, the deviation from criticality $t =  eta_c -  eta$, and the coupling strength $ eta$.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on several advanced inequalities (e.g., correlation inequalities, Griffiths–Kelly–Sherman inequalities) and involves conjectures regarding the RFIM limit.
paper_structure: The paper develops bounds on correlation functions and partition functions using various inequalities (e.g., Lemma 5.1, Lemma 5.2) to ultimately establish the quantitative relationship between the two gaps.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the rigorous comparison of spectral gaps (mass gap vs. Lee-Yang gap) provides deep mathematical tools applicable to understanding spectral properties in quantum many-body systems, especially near critical points.
